S17.01.needs: a sent answer in a chat
S17.01.note: The assistant name is not a fixed label; it comes from the model label helper, so the exact words vary by model. Screen-reader naming was not checked.
steps: Sign in and open a chat that already has an answer, or send one question and wait for the answer.
Move the mouse over the answer's bottom action line, under the answer text.
Look for the small model text that appears on hover, for example 'Auto chose ...' or the model name, and compare with Expected: the answer is distinguishable from your message and names the model.
S17.01.where: Any answer in a chat > hover over the answer's bottom line (the small model name text, for example 'Auto chose ...' when Auto picked the model)

S17.02.needs: a working model route that returns text
S17.02.note: Streaming is inner behaviour; the code that renders incrementally is in StreamingMarkdownContent. Whether it actually streams depends on the model route.
steps: Send any question in a chat.
Watch the answer area below your message while the reply is generated.
Check that the text grows piece by piece and that bold, lists and code blocks show as formatted text, as Expected says.
S17.02.where: The answer area while a reply is being generated, after you press Send

S17.03.note: 'New chat' is the label of the new-chat control in the chat page; the sidebar position was not mapped.
steps: Open a new chat and type any question.
Press Send.
Look just below your message for a spinning mark with the word 'Preparing', and for the status phrase 'Generating response' (announced to screen readers only).
Compare with Expected: a visible working indicator appears before or while the text arrives.
S17.03.where: New chat > type a message > Send, then look below your message for 'Preparing'

S17.04.needs: a model that returns thinking steps
S17.04.note: The row only appears when the answer has thinking steps; it is not shown for all models.
steps: Send a question to a model that produces reasoning (choose a reasoning model in the model picker).
When the answer finishes, look under it for a row starting with 'Thinking process'.
Click the row to expand it.
Compare with Expected: a collapsible list of the reasoning steps appears and collapses again on a second click.
S17.04.where: A reasoning-capable answer > under the answer, click 'Thinking process (N steps)'

S17.05.needs: a request that makes the assistant use a tool
S17.05.note: The per-tool name, status and result fields were not individually traced to visible words.
steps: Send a question that makes the assistant use a tool (for example a web search or a file tool).
When the answer finishes, look for the tool timeline row under the answer.
Click the row (its toggle is labelled 'Toggle tool timeline') to expand it.
Compare with Expected: each tool's name, status and result appear inside.
S17.05.where: An answer that used a tool > click the tool timeline row under the answer

labels.text: Project files used in this answer

S17.06.needs: web search or project files that produce citations
S17.06.note: The numbered marker has no fixed visible words in the code; its label is built per source. The label listed is for project-file citations only.
steps: Send a question that needs current information, such as a news question, with web search on.
When the answer finishes, look for small numbered markers in the answer text.
Click one marker.
Compare with Expected: it opens or points to the source the claim came from.
S17.06.where: An answer that used web search > click a numbered citation marker in the answer text

S17.07.needs: a request that uses web search
S17.07.note: The sources list itself is a separate control (SourcesControl) whose visible words were not traced.
steps: Send a question that uses web search and wait for the answer to finish.
Look at the row under the answer, at the right side.
Click the button labelled 'Show sources' (its tooltip says 'Sources').
Compare with Expected: a list of the sources used opens and can be read and opened.
S17.07.where: An answer that used web search > the row under the answer > 'Show sources' button (tooltip 'Sources')

S17.08.needs: a request that creates a file
S17.08.note: File type and name display were not traced to visible words.
steps: Ask AGI to create a file, for example a document.
When the answer finishes, look for a file card under the answer, grouped with the label 'Files this session produced'.
Click 'Download generated file' on the card (or 'Share generated file').
Compare with Expected: the card shows the file name and type, and the download works.
S17.08.where: An answer that produced a file > the file card under the answer > 'Download generated file'

S17.09.needs: a request that creates an artifact
S17.09.note: The overflow label is a template; the exact count text is built at runtime.
steps: Ask for something that creates an artifact, for example a small web page or an SVG drawing.
When the answer finishes, look for the card group labelled 'Artifacts' under the answer.
Click one card.
Compare with Expected: the artifact opens in the artifact panel or viewer.
S17.09.where: An answer that created a web page, React component or SVG > click the artifact card under the answer

S17.10.needs: an account and model route that can generate images
S17.10.note: Whether a given account can generate images was not checked; the download button label is built from the media kind.
steps: Ask for an image, for example 'draw a red bicycle'.
Wait for the card labelled 'Generating image' to finish.
Click the image to open it, then use the 'Download' control.
Compare with Expected: the image shows inline in the answer and downloads.
S17.10.where: An answer that generated an image > click the image card in the answer > 'Download' (image card button labelled 'Download image')

S17.12.note: Video generation is gated by tool type and account; availability was not checked.
steps: Ask for a video using video generation.
Wait for the video in the answer to finish; a failure shows 'Video generation ended' or 'Video failed to load'.
Press play on the video player labelled 'Generated video', then check the controls.
Click 'Download video' and compare with Expected: the video plays inline with controls and downloads.
S17.12.where: An answer that generated a video > the video player in the answer > 'Download video'

S17.13.needs: a request that makes the model return a card
S17.13.note: InteractiveCardBlock.tsx renders model-produced cards, but the on-screen controls depend on the card kind and their visible words were not mapped. I searched apps/web/features/chat/components/messages for card components and found the fallback section only.

S17.14.needs: a settings toggle and a finished answer
S17.14.note: The feature is off by default: FOLLOW_UP_SUGGESTIONS_ENABLED_DEFAULT is false in ChatMessageList.tsx, so no suggestions show until the toggle is on. The General section tab name was not confirmed.
steps: Open Settings and go to the General section.
Turn on 'Show follow-up suggestions in chats'.
Open a chat, send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Look under the answer for suggested follow-up prompts and click one; compare with Expected.
S17.14.where: Settings > General > 'Show follow-up suggestions in chats' (switch on), then look under an answer in a chat

S17.15.note: The tooltip word is 'Copy'; the aria label is 'Copy message'.
steps: Open a chat with a finished answer.
Hover over the answer's action row and click 'Copy message' (the copy icon).
Paste into a text field in another app, for example Notes.
Compare with Expected: the whole answer text is pasted, and the button label changes to 'Message copied' briefly.
S17.15.where: Any answer > action row under the answer > 'Copy message' (tooltip 'Copy')

S17.17.needs: a finished answer and audio output
S17.17.note: The menu item is a checkbox item; the spoken output depends on the device.
steps: Open a chat with a finished answer.
Click the button labelled 'More message actions' in the answer's action row.
Click 'Read message aloud'.
Compare with Expected: the answer is spoken aloud.
S17.17.where: Any answer > action row > 'More message actions' > 'Read message aloud'

S17.18.needs: a finished answer and audio output
S17.18.note: The chat list also stops playback when the conversation changes.
steps: Start 'Read message aloud' on an answer, as in S17.17.
While it is speaking, open 'More message actions' on the same answer.
Click 'Stop reading message'.
Compare with Expected: the speech stops and the menu item returns to 'Read message aloud'.
S17.18.where: While an answer is being read aloud > 'More message actions' > 'Stop reading message'

S17.19.note: A regenerated attempt is kept as another variant (see S17.28).
steps: Open a chat with a finished answer.
Hover over the action row and click 'Regenerate response'.
Wait for the new attempt to appear for the same prompt.
Compare with Expected: a new attempt for the same question replaces the answer in place.
S17.19.where: Any finished answer > action row > 'Regenerate response' (circular arrow, tooltip 'Regenerate')

S17.20.needs: a way to make the turn fail
S17.20.note: The retry control appears in the chat list notice, not in the message action row.
steps: Send a message that fails (for example when the model route is unavailable).
Look at the notice below the failed answer and click 'Retry' (aria label 'Retry this response').
Wait for the new outcome.
Compare with Expected: the failure is replaced by the new result for the same turn.
S17.20.where: A failed answer > the notice under the answer > 'Retry'

S17.21.needs: a request that hits the output limit
S17.21.note: Whether a given model truncates is not checked; the button only shows when the answer can be continued.
steps: Send a request that needs a long answer, for example 'write a long essay'.
If the answer stops at the output limit, look below it for 'Continue generating'.
Click it.
Compare with Expected: the same answer resumes and continues from where it stopped.
S17.21.where: A truncated answer > the button below it 'Continue generating'

S17.22.needs: more than one model option available on the account
S17.22.note: The dropdown only appears when there are model options; the notice above a failed turn also has 'Switch model'.
steps: Open a chat with a finished answer that has model options.
Click the 'Regenerate response' control that has a dropdown.
Under 'Try again with', click another model name.
Compare with Expected: a new attempt is produced with that model in one step.
S17.22.where: Any finished answer > action row > 'Regenerate response' dropdown arrow > 'Try again with' > pick a model

labels.text: Branch conversation: this chat stays unchanged

S17.27.needs: a chat with at least two exchanges
S17.27.note: The button is hidden in voice mode.
steps: Open a chat with several messages.
Hover over an answer's action row and click 'Branch conversation from here'.
Wait for 'Creating branch…' to finish.
Compare with Expected: a new conversation holds the history up to that answer, and the original chat is unchanged.
S17.27.where: Any answer > action row > 'Branch conversation from here' (fork icon, tooltip 'Branch conversation: this chat stays unchanged')

S17.28.note: The pager is disabled while the chat is streaming, and it shows only when there are two or more attempts.
steps: Regenerate an answer (see S17.19) so the same question has two or more responses.
Look for the small arrows beside the answer; the middle text reads 'Response N of M'.
Click 'Next response' and 'Previous response' to page between attempts.
Compare with Expected: the answer text changes to the other attempt and the count updates.
S17.28.where: An answer with two or more attempts > the arrows beside the answer ('Previous response' / 'Next response')

S17.29.note: Whether the rating is stored against the message was not checked.
steps: Open a chat with a finished answer.
Hover over the action row and click the thumbs-up 'Good response'.
Check that the button now shows 'Remove rating' and is pressed.
Compare with Expected: positive feedback is recorded for that answer.
S17.29.where: Any finished answer > action row > thumbs up 'Good response'

S17.30.note: Whether a details panel opens after thumbs-down was not traced; ResponseRatingDetails.tsx is the component that may show it.
steps: Open a chat with a finished answer.
Hover over the action row and click the thumbs-down 'Bad response'.
Check whether a details panel opens (ResponseRatingDetails) and whether the button shows 'Remove rating'.
Compare with Expected: negative feedback is recorded for that answer.
S17.30.where: Any finished answer > action row > thumbs down 'Bad response'

S17.31.note: The report defaults to the 'harmful' category; no category picker was seen in this code path.
steps: Open a chat with a finished answer.
Click 'More message actions' in the action row.
Click 'Report this response'.
Compare with Expected: the item changes to 'Reporting…' and then 'Reported', and the report is filed for that answer.
S17.31.where: Any finished answer > action row > 'More message actions' > 'Report this response'

S17.32.needs: a signed-in account with a chat that has at least one message; the answer share uses the system share sheet where the browser provides one
S17.32.note: The header button is labelled "Share" in visible text and "Share conversation" in its accessible name; the dialog has a workspace audience option too, which I did not trace further.
steps: Open or start a chat and send one message so the chat has messages.
Click the "Share conversation" button in the top bar (on wide windows it reads "Share").
In the dialog "Share conversation", leave the expiry at 7 days and click "Create public link".
Look for the link to appear with a "Copy" button and check it opens the same conversation.
For one answer: hover it, click "More message actions", then click "Share answer" and look for the system share sheet or an error toast "This answer could not be shared".
S17.32.where: Top bar of a chat that has messages > "Share conversation" button (text "Share" shows on wide windows) > dialog "Share conversation" > "Create public link · 7 days" (or "Copy" once a link exists). Per answer: hover the answer, open "More message actions" > "Share answer".

S17.36.needs: a completed answer from a route that sends token counts (not every provider sends them)
S17.36.note: The usage block has no fixed heading. It appears only when the answer carries token counts, and its wording comes from the TokenUsageDisplay component; the model name under the answer is data, not a fixed label.
steps: Send a message and wait for the answer to finish.
Hover the answer and look for the name of the model under it.
Click the "More message actions" button under the answer.
Scroll to the bottom of the menu, below the separator, and look for the token usage block and a time in seconds such as "2.4s".
Compare the model shown there with the Expected: which model answered and its usage.
S17.36.where: Any answer > "More message actions" (the three-dot button under the answer) > the usage block at the bottom of the menu (tokens, model, request id, seconds). The model name is also shown under the answer on hover as the answered-by label.

labels.text: the part that arrived is kept above

S17.37.needs: a provider failure after output has started; this cannot be made on demand from the UI
S17.37.note: The reason line is only shown on the turn's status row when the answer had run activity; with no activity it is a single row "Response failed: <reason>" from MessageBubble.tsx. The reasons for an interrupted turn are in a map in ChatMessageList.tsx. I did not verify a live reproduction.
steps: Send a message that a provider fails partway through (for example by a provider outage or a timeout).
Look at the answer: the text that arrived should still be there, above a status line.
Read the status line: it should say "Response failed" followed by the reason, or "Response finished with errors".
Compare with Expected: the partial text must be kept and clearly marked incomplete, with the reason.
S17.37.where: A chat whose answer fails after some text has already arrived > the answer keeps its text above a status line "Response failed" (with the reason after it), or "Response cancelled. Partial response saved.", or "Response finished with errors".

labels.text: The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons.

S17.38.needs: a prompt that triggers a provider safety refusal; this cannot be forced from the UI
S17.38.note: The notice shows only when the last finish reason is a refusal or content filter. I did not find a separate refusal label for the status row.
steps: Send a prompt that the model's safety layer refuses (the app cannot choose this on demand).
Look under the answer for the notice "The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons."
Check that it is not styled as an ordinary answer or a generic error.
Click "Report issue" and look for the feedback dialog that opens for a safety appeal.
Compare with Expected: a distinct refusal state with a next step.
S17.38.where: An answer that the safety layer stops > the notice "The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons." with a "Report issue" button under it.

S17.39.needs: none for a Free account; a message with a long answer so you have time to press stop
S17.39.note: The stop button has no visible word, only its accessible name. A stopped turn also gets the status line "Response cancelled. Partial response saved." from ChatMessageList.tsx. I did not verify the stop control live.
steps: Send a message that gives a long answer.
While the answer is still streaming, click the stop button (accessible name "Stop the current response").
Look under the answer for "Response stopped." and check the text that already arrived is still shown.
Click "Try again" and compare with Expected: the answer is marked stopped, keeps what arrived, and offers to try again.
S17.39.where: Send a message > click the stop control while the answer is still being written > the answer shows "Response stopped." with a "Try again" button under it.

S17.40.needs: a model route that returns an empty response; this cannot be forced from the UI
S17.40.note: The same reason text also exists in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/errors.json. The error-state wording is built in ChatMessageList.tsx and MessageBubble.tsx, and I did not reproduce it live.
steps: Send a message to a model route that returns no text (the app cannot choose this on demand).
Look for an explicit status line "Response failed" with the reason "no response was returned.", not an empty answer bubble.
Check that a "Retry" button is shown with it.
Click "Retry" and compare the new outcome with Expected: an explicit no-response error with retry, not an empty bubble.
S17.40.where: A turn that returns nothing > the answer row shows "Response failed: no response was returned." with a "Retry" button.
